topic_title: Amino Acids — Zwitterions and Isoelectric Point

notes_list.title: Amino Acids — Zwitterions and Isoelectric Point
notes_list.basic_overview: Amino acids contain amino and carboxyl groups and often exist as zwitterions near neutral pH. Their acid-base behavior is described by pKa values and isoelectric point.
notes_list.extra_info_content: At low pH the amino acid is more protonated; at intermediate pH the zwitterion dominates; at high pH the carboxylate and amino group can both be deprotonated. For simple neutral side chains, pI ≈ average of pKa values bracketing the zwitterion.
notes_list.examples: Glycine is the simplest amino acid. Acidic and basic side chains require choosing the correct pair of pKa values for pI calculation.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Aqueous buffered medium; ionic strength can affect measured pKa values.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Identify ionizable groups. 2. Order pKa values. 3. Determine dominant charge as pH changes. 4. Average the two pKa values around net-zero form for simple cases.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Acid-base equilibria are thermodynamic; electrophoretic mobility near pI approaches zero because net charge is near zero.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not blindly average all pKa values; use the two that bracket the neutral species.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
must_revise: pI = (pKa1+pKa2)/2 for simple neutral amino acid
